statement: Nothing for itch.io exists: no page set-up note, key procedure, channel names, upload script or rehearsal record (the same hole as TOOLS F-TOOLS-02, seen from the distribution side).
evidence: git grep -i -E 'itch\.io|\bbutler\b' -- tools .github net render ui sim: one test string, ui/tools/hud_check.gd:9416 (read 2026-11-13)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (upload script, channel list, version string, a rehearsal with a dummy build, a one-page checklist for the owner's own actions)
depends_on: TOOLS F-TOOLS-01 (a Windows and a Linux build of the game as played); F-MARKET-08 (title)
risk: The rehearsal cannot start until the owner has made the account and page; two itch.io behaviours (whether a key needs an account, how a tester goes back a version) are known only from forum threads.
orb_question: Will you create the itch.io account and the key-only page, and install its upload tool, yourself once Tools has a one-page checklist? Recommendation: yes, in one sitting.

statement: There is no fixed shot list: the recipe file covers three of the six named shots and has no recipe for a transformation, a lap of the globe or a LAN 2v2 moment.
cost_basis: adds rows and one or two hook scenes to a kit whose whole build was estimated at 0.5 to 0.8M tokens (docs/tools/clip-capture-audit.md:34; its real cost is not recorded)
risk: A shot whose scene writes into the sim (as the hook's staged scenes do) is not a played match; the list should say which shots are staged.

statement: No job renders the shots at a milestone and no archive exists: clips land in a git-ignored folder with no milestone name, no line on what changed and no backup.
evidence: homework/Files/clips/ holds one folder, mms-2026-11-10 (local, git-ignored; read 2026-11-13)
git ls-files | grep -i changelog: no file (read 2026-11-13)
risk: Everything kept so far is on one disk; a lost disk loses every earlier milestone's footage and builds.
orb_question: Where is the progress archive kept safe? Recommendation: a second disk or a private folder you already have, copied at each milestone.

statement: The capture hook exists only in a browser build, so the Alpha candidate's own Windows and Linux programs cannot be filmed, and a LAN 2v2 shot depends on a replay route whose self-test is in no workflow and which has not yet read a real LAN save.
evidence: grep of .github/workflows/*.yml for lan-clip-selftest: no line (read 2026-11-13)
docs/ep/alpha/audit-2026-11-13/questions.md:16 (AQ-01, Tools: the first real LAN save through lan-report is owed)
depends_on: TOOLS F-TOOLS-01 (one build that holds solo and LAN)
risk: The archive would show a browser picture of a game testers play as a desktop program; nothing compares the two pictures.

statement: Footage is made at 960 by 540, shrunk to 480 wide at 12 pictures a second, as GIF or browser-recorded WebM with no MP4, below what the project's own Steam note asks of screenshots and a trailer.
evidence: docs/marketing/steam-readiness.md:15-16 (the platform's sizes: needs web check)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the picture size is a recipe key and PNG sequences already exist; a full-size run through the launcher's CPU cap is untimed)
risk: Alpha's footage, kept only as small GIFs, cannot be used in a later video; a full-size capture may be slow under the 25% CPU cap.
orb_question: May Tools ask you to install a free video encoder when the first teaser is cut? Recommendation: not now; keep full-size picture sequences until Beta is in sight.

statement: Only GIFs get the flash check; WebM video and PNG sequences leave the kit with no verdict, and no page says how a public video is screened.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the analyser already reads frames; the kit keeps the frames a WebM is made from)
risk: A 15-second clip mark is cut as WebM by default (tools/clips/clips.json:38), so the clips most likely to be passed to a friend are the unscreened ones.

statement: No tester guide says how a tester gets a key, installs on a Steam Deck, updates, or posts a report; the only tester page is Legal's note, which does not mention itch.io.
evidence: git ls-files | grep -i tester: docs/legal/alpha-tester-note.md only (read 2026-11-13)
depends_on: F-MARKET-01 (the real steps are known only after the rehearsal)
risk: A guide written before the rehearsal will describe steps nobody has done on a Deck.

statement: Legal's own page puts the formal title search before any itch.io page, the title row is still open, and nothing excuses a key-only page (the same point as LEGAL F-LEGAL-09).
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (one Legal row; a paid search is the owner's spend, not tokens)
risk: The page is made under a title that later has to change, and every key and guide carries the old one.
orb_question: May the key-only page go up under the working title before the paid title search? Recommendation: yes, only if Legal first writes one row saying an unlisted, unpromoted, key-only page is acceptable.

statement: The clips shared so far were staged on a private test copy with behaviour the game does not have (both at top power, a beam on a button, changed speeds, a scratch-only camera), so they cannot be remade from main and are not the game as played.
evidence: homework/Files/clips/mms-2026-11-10/index.txt (local, git-ignored; section 'What is not stock gameplay')
git grep -l mmcam: only docs/tools/pending/mms-tweaks/ and docs/tools/runs/mms-2026-11-10/ (read 2026-11-13)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (a rule in the shot list: stock build, stock inputs, real speed, each shot labelled staged or played)
risk: A staged clip used publicly would show moves a player cannot do; two milestones would differ for reasons that are not progress.

statement: No rule says what happens to a shot when an old replay stops playing: a replay is refused on different data, and the page word that plays a saved match is a scratch patch, not game code on main.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the rule: a shot is a script of scene, seed and inputs, re-recorded on each milestone; a played replay is kept with its own build)
risk: Shots built on saved replays vanish at the first data change; shots built on recipes survive.

statement: The marketing plan predates Orb's Alpha definition: it stages a public browser build and public itch.io page, advises against Discord, still holds clips for the old placeholder names, and has no timeline counting back from the Steam demo.
risk: A director briefed from the old plan builds toward a public page the owner has not asked for.
orb_question: What should 'Beta in sight' mean, the point where the Steam clock starts? Recommendation: four fighters playable on the Windows and Linux builds and the Alpha testers' reports folded in.

statement: The project's notes disagree with each other on Valve's waiting period and are stale on the licence: three records name different pages for the 21 and 30 days, and two Legal pages still call the code MIT.
risk: Planning on 30 days is safe under every reading; the risk is someone acting on the stale licence line.

statement: The self-tests of the clip kit, the browser launcher and the LAN clip tool run in no workflow, so the chain the archive depends on can break unseen.
evidence: grep of .github/workflows/*.yml for clips-selftest, machine/selftest, lan-clip-selftest: no line (read 2026-11-13)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (the halves that need no browser only)
risk: A CI job that starts a browser capture adds minutes and a new way to hang; only the non-browser halves belong there.

statement: Bystanders' run cycles follow the shader's clock, not the tick, so two renders of the same shot differ in the crowd and a side-by-side shows a difference that is not a change in the game.
risk: A change to the crowd's clock alters the picture, so it needs the look gate's side-by-side.

statement: A player cannot hide the HUD and there is no photo mode; both are absent from the game and neither is in Orb's Alpha definition.
orb_question: Photo mode after Alpha? Recommendation: yes, after Alpha; the scripted shot list does not need it.

statement: One command makes seeded, repeatable clips from a kept build out of one recipe file, finding moments from the sim's own events, and six clips made on 2026-11-10 are on record.
Every clip tool starts its browser through the one guarded launcher, which sets a hard time limit, below-normal priority, a CPU cap and a profile named for its session.
A replay reproduces a match from its seed and intents, is refused on different data, and the clip made from a saved match says whether its checkpoints matched the match that was played.
The side-by-side tool pairs two captured clips as labelled stills and a GIF and refuses a pair that is not the same scenario and seed.
Capture is clean in a browser build: the hook shows no card, notice or intro, a page word hides the HUD without touching the sim, and the kit uses it by default.
Capture pacing is even whatever the PC is doing: the hook runs exactly one tick per picture.
A clip button (F9, or View and RB) and automatic bookmarks mark moments in a saved match, and the kit cuts a clip for each from the replay.
Each build the owner played is kept by commit (18 folders), which is the build half of a milestone archive.
evidence: homework/Files/builds/ (local, git-ignored; 18 folders, newest orb-first-play-6a30b4c9-6627cb9d and orb-lan-6a30b4c9; read 2026-11-13)

statement: The owner's rules for public material are written where the work will be done: real captures only, no in-progress character art, the AI wording for video descriptions, and publishing held for the owner's approval.

The project's Steam planning figures are on the safe side of the platform pages read on 2026-11-13: 30 days from the fee, two weeks of coming soon, seven business days per review, and a free game never recoups the fee.
